_schema.source: HANDOFF-PACKAGE.md §4 (Win Theme Library, 30 themes for DM-904)
_schema.note: Reusable win-theme library Digital Mary draws from when coaching a capture pursuit. Mapped to typical federal health IT scenarios. Author: Mary Womack via OpenClaw Digital Mary handoff.

themes.name: Modular Delivery Sprint
themes.applies_when: Customer demands rapid capability fielding inside a long IDIQ
themes.message: We deliver value in 90-day sprints, not 18-month waterfalls — the customer sees working capability before next quarter's ART planning
themes.anti_pattern: Generic 'Agile' claims with no cadence proof

themes.name: Onramp-in-30
themes.applies_when: Customer has been burned by 6-month transition pain
themes.message: Full operational transition in 30 calendar days with zero capability gap to the incumbent
themes.anti_pattern: Promising fast onramp without naming the retention strategy

themes.name: Decision-Velocity Advantage
themes.applies_when: Slow incumbent is missing customer windows
themes.message: Our flat decision authority means a customer ask Monday morning has a yes/no by Wednesday — not a 30-day change request
themes.anti_pattern: Vague 'responsive' language

themes.name: Smaller is Faster
themes.applies_when: Competing as small biz vs giant prime
themes.message: No matrix layers between SOW and execution — your contracting officer talks to the person doing the work
themes.anti_pattern: Apologizing for being small

themes.name: Pre-Mobilized Bench
themes.applies_when: Customer has urgent staffing need
themes.message: Cleared, credentialed, MHS-experienced staff ready to badge-in within 10 days — not 90
themes.anti_pattern: Listing resume names without confirming availability

themes.name: DHA-Native Past Performance
themes.applies_when: Customer is DHA and weighting DHA-specific PP heavily
themes.message: Five active DHA contracts in the last 36 months — we operate inside DHA, not adjacent to it
themes.anti_pattern: Citing generic DoD or commercial PP and calling it equivalent

themes.name: Health-IT-Only Focus
themes.applies_when: Competing against a generalist prime
themes.message: 100% of our revenue is federal health IT — we don't borrow attention from civilian or commercial portfolios
proofs_required: Executive bios scoped to health IT
themes.anti_pattern: Claiming focus when LinkedIn shows broad portfolio

themes.name: Clinical-Operator Insight
themes.applies_when: SOW touches clinical workflow (MHS GENESIS optimization, etc.)
themes.message: Our team includes [N] former MTF clinical operators who have used the system in care delivery, not just designed for it
proofs_required: Named staff with MTF clinical roles
themes.anti_pattern: Listing clinical advisors who haven't touched a patient in a decade

themes.name: Federal EHR Coordination Fluency
themes.applies_when: Buy touches FEHRM-coordinated workstreams
themes.message: We've operated on both sides — DoD and VA — of the Federal EHR, so we deliver across the seam, not from one side of it
themes.anti_pattern: DoD-only or VA-only past performance claiming joint expertise

themes.name: Mission-Read Roadmap
themes.applies_when: Customer has explicit mission priorities (DHA Strategic Plan, VA EHRM milestones)
themes.message: Our solution maps each capability directly to a published [DHA/VA] strategic priority — section, page, line
proofs_required: Mapping table from solution to strategic doc paragraphs
themes.anti_pattern: Generic 'aligned with mission' language

themes.name: Open-by-Default Architecture (MOSA)
themes.applies_when: SOW invokes MOSA or vendor-lock concerns
themes.message: Open standards (HL7 FHIR, OpenAPI, OCI) are the default — no proprietary glue that locks the customer into us
themes.anti_pattern: Claiming MOSA while shipping proprietary connectors

themes.name: AI Governance Maturity
themes.applies_when: AI/ML is in scope post-2025 EO
themes.message: NIST AI RMF documentation, model cards, and bias-testing artifacts ship as deliverables — not afterthoughts
themes.anti_pattern: 'We follow NIST AI RMF' without concrete artifact samples

themes.name: FedRAMP-Ready Stack
themes.applies_when: Cloud delivery is in scope
themes.message: Production stack is FedRAMP Moderate / High authorized — not 'in process,' authorized
themes.anti_pattern: Naming 'FedRAMP-aligned' or 'FedRAMP-ready' instead of authorized

themes.name: Data-First Engineering
themes.applies_when: Buy touches Advana, HCDS, or analytics
themes.message: Data products land in Advana on day one — not an afterthought migration in year two
themes.anti_pattern: Claiming Advana fluency without prior deliveries

themes.name: Zero-Trust Native
themes.applies_when: Customer cybersecurity priorities are visible
themes.message: Solution architecture is zero-trust from day one (per OMB M-22-09 / DoD ZT Strategy) — not bolt-on remediation
themes.anti_pattern: Generic 'secure by design'

themes.name: DCAA-Audited Discipline
themes.applies_when: Cost-realism evaluation is heavy
themes.message: Our forward pricing rates are DCAA-approved and cost-realism-tested across [N] prior cost-reimbursable awards — your evaluators won't adjust us up
themes.anti_pattern: Underbidding without showing the audit posture

themes.name: Risk-Adjusted Pricing
themes.applies_when: Customer is risk-averse after a prior failed program
themes.message: Fixed-price firm where we can; cost-plus only where the work is genuinely undefined — and we'll show you which is which line by line
themes.anti_pattern: Race-to-the-bottom on every CLIN

themes.name: Transparent ODC Posture
themes.applies_when: Travel and ODCs matter (regional services)
themes.message: ODC and travel estimates built bottom-up from the SOW, not borrowed from a competitor's prior bid — and reconciled to the customer's IGCE
themes.anti_pattern: Round-number ODCs that look made up

themes.name: Insourced Continuity
themes.applies_when: Customer has been hurt by sub turnover
themes.message: [X]% of work performed by W-2 employees — not 1099s or sub-of-a-sub — so the team you evaluate is the team that delivers
themes.anti_pattern: Claiming continuity while leaning heavily on subs

themes.name: Capped-Risk Backstop
themes.applies_when: Customer fears cost overruns
themes.message: Cost-plus award fee with our share line steeper than baseline — we lose more than the customer if we overrun
themes.anti_pattern: Vague 'skin in the game' claims

themes.name: Named Key Personnel
themes.applies_when: Section L names key personnel
themes.message: Every key personnel resume names a real person currently on staff with letter of commitment — no ghost résumés
themes.anti_pattern: 'TBD' or 'to be hired' key roles

themes.name: Clearance Density
themes.applies_when: Cleared work is the bulk of the SOW
themes.message: [X]% of proposed staff already hold the required clearances — no clearance ramp risk
themes.anti_pattern: Counting recruitable cleared personnel as if they're already on staff

themes.name: Diverse Sourcing Network
themes.applies_when: Customer values supply chain diversity (small biz, set-aside flow-down)
themes.message: Our subcontract plan flows [X]% to small business and [Y]% to specific set-aside categories — exceeding the customer's goals
themes.anti_pattern: Generic small-biz commitment without named partners

themes.name: Customer-Facing Continuity
themes.applies_when: Long PoP and customer cares about turnover
themes.message: Our project leadership turnover on comparable contracts averages [X]% — not [Y]% industry baseline
proofs_required: Tenure data on comparable PWS leads
themes.anti_pattern: Selling stability without showing turnover numbers

themes.name: Cross-Tier Bench
themes.applies_when: SOW spans junior to senior labor categories
themes.message: We staff senior architects to entry analysts from a single integrated bench — no cobbled subs at every labor band
themes.anti_pattern: Heavy sub usage at junior bands undermining unified-team claim

themes.name: Outcome SLAs over LOE
themes.applies_when: Customer is shifting from LOE to outcomes
themes.message: We propose mission-outcome SLAs (system uptime, time-to-deploy, user-satisfaction) — not just hours billed
themes.anti_pattern: Outcome talk paired with LOE pricing

themes.name: Operational Tempo Match
themes.applies_when: Customer cadence is rapid (DHA J-6 sprints, etc.)
themes.message: Our delivery cadence matches the customer's tempo — weekly demos in their stand-ups, not quarterly briefings
themes.anti_pattern: Imposing a vendor cadence on the customer

themes.name: End-User Satisfaction Track Record
themes.applies_when: Clinician/end-user satisfaction is a stated goal
themes.message: End-user CSAT on prior MHS GENESIS optimization work averaged [X]/10 — measured, not asserted
themes.anti_pattern: Generic 'user-centered' without measured outcome

themes.name: Continuous Improvement Loop
themes.applies_when: Customer wants ongoing learning, not one-time delivery
themes.message: Built-in retrospectives feed quarterly capability roadmap updates — the contract gets better quarter over quarter, not just delivered
themes.anti_pattern: 'Lessons learned' without showing how they shaped follow-on work

themes.name: Sustainable Knowledge Transfer
themes.applies_when: Customer fears vendor lock-in to your team
themes.message: Government-owned artifacts (runbooks, code, data models) updated continuously and reviewed quarterly with the COR — the customer can swap us out at any option year
themes.anti_pattern: KT only at end of PoP
